summary.text: Melanie Stansbury is the Democratic incumbent for New Mexico's 1st Congressional District, first elected in a June 2021 special election to succeed Deb Haaland.

Before Congress she worked as a science educator and researcher on land and water issues, on the staff of the Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee and at the White House Office of Management and Budget, and served one term in the New Mexico House of Representatives. Her official biography highlights work on water, hunger, conservation, climate change and economic development.

paragraphs.text: Stansbury was born in Farmington, New Mexico, and her official biography says she was born and raised in New Mexico.
She earned a bachelor's degree in human ecology and natural science from Saint Mary's College of California in 2002 and a master's in development sociology from Cornell University in 2007.

Before entering elected office, she worked in communities across New Mexico as a STEM educator and researcher on land and water issues and held staff roles at the U.S. Senate Committee on Energy and Natural Resources and the White House Office of Management and Budget. Ballotpedia also lists the New Mexico Museum of Natural History and Science and consulting work.

Stansbury won election to the New Mexico House of Representatives (District 28) in 2018, defeating incumbent Jimmie Hall, and served from 2019 to 2021. In the state House she was vice chair of the Energy, Environment and Natural Resources Committee and sat on the Taxation and Revenue Committee in 2021-2022.
She won the June 1, 2021 special general election for the 1st District seat vacated by Deb Haaland, with 60.4% of the vote.

In the U.S. House, Stansbury serves on the Committee on Natural Resources (Federal Lands, and Water, Wildlife, and Fisheries subcommittees) and the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform (Subcommittee on Delivering on Government Efficiency).
Her office lists her as vice chair of the Congressional Native American Caucus, co-chair of the Wildlife Refuge Caucus and a Member Services Task Force co-chair of the Democratic Women's Caucus.
She advanced from the June 2, 2026 Democratic primary for the seat.
